newsitem.title: CANADA: Teck sees '97 gold output of 380,000 oz.
newsitem.headline: Teck sees '97 gold output of 380,000 oz.

text.p: Teck Corp said on Wednesday that it expected its gold production in 1997 to rise to 380,000 ounces from 360,000 ounces in 1996.
Company officials told the annual meeting that the increased output would come partly from its mining operations in western Australia.
The company said recent feasibility studies suggested that Teck could produce up to 675,000 ounces of gold by 2000.
Teck CFO John Taylor declined to forecast 1997 earnings, saying that while overall metals production this year will be similar to 1996, financial results are sensitive to metal prices.

"We are bullish on gold prices, (although in the short term) the threat of central banks sales will have a dampening effect on the market," he said, adding that the company expected a long-term increase in gold prices.
Teck last week reported first-uarter net earnings of $15 million on a mine operating profit of $50 million.
Teck President Norman Keevil said the company's priority was to use its solid financial position to develop new projects in Ontario, Chile, Australia and Mexico.

A feasibility study for the company's Lobo-Marte gold properties in Chile should be completed by the end of 1997, Keevil said. Reserves at the site are estimated to be 4.3 million ounces, with Teck's share amounting to between 2.2 million and 2.6 milllion ounces.
In 1997 Teck expects to produce 133,000 pounds of copper, 69,000 pounds of zinc and 13,000 pounds of lead.
